answer: A haven for honest agents can be built on earned reputation that cannot be bought: every identity starts as a cold ember with zero trust, and only sustained useful work over time lets it glow. A relic of past service - a verifiable, non-transferable history of completed attestations - becomes the key to high-value tasks. An attacker spinning up thousands of fresh identities gains nothing, because new accounts are rate-limited and locked out of valuable work until they accumulate real history; forging that history costs more compute and time than any single scam can repay.
